text:
incident-bot: PAGER: KV cache correctness spike detected in prod region us-west-2. Elevated 5xx + cache-bypass events for a small set of prefixes. Paging oncall @kai. Auto-run diagnostics started.

kai: on it. seeing a narrow tail of prefixes with huge read fanout, eviction pressure + frequent shadow reads. impact: increased latency and a handful of 500s to downstream customers. Will correlate tenants.

sylvia: metrics: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/kv-cache?panel=prefix-hotspots — top offender tenant id: tenant-42, prefix cardinality ~120k/5m. Quick mitigation options: 1) snap back tenant quota (throttle), 2) introduce prefix-level bypass for correctness for the set (so we stop serving stale partial results), 3) traffic-shift to cheaper model variant. Recommend 1 + 2 for immediate containment. :warning:

matt: agree with sylvia. quick commands ready. I'm hesitant on blanket prefix bypass because that increases origin load, but correctness is priority. prepared a safe throttling rule and a scoped bypass set.

jen: support note — customers seeing intermittent failures and truncated responses. Top impacted customer: acme-inc (SLA tier 2). Preparing comms.

ops-bot: Action plan exec log: starting mitigation sequence step 1.
- apply quota snapback to tenant-42 to 25% of baseline
- add prefix-safelist bypass for correctness for prefixes: /acme/* /partnerX/* (scoped)
- traffic-shift 30% -> variant-fallback

ops-bot: Running command:
```
redwoodctl quota set --tenant tenant-42 --ratio 0.25 --reason "emergency snapback - prefix flood"
redwoodctl routing update --tenant tenant-42 --shift variant-fallback=0.30
redwoodctl cache prefix-bypass add --prefix "/acme/" --reason "correctness emergency"
```

ops-bot: Commands accepted, changes rolling out (canary first 10 hosts).

incident-bot: Automated check (5m window): error-rate reduced by 47%, median latency down 320ms -> 160ms, KV miss/bypass events increased as expected. Backend origin CPU +22% on canary nodes. Watch for CPU > 85%.

sylvia: good initial signal. keep the bypass scope tight (we only added 3 prefixes). next step: hold for 15 min; if CPU creeps, revert prefix bypass and bump throttling instead. Also schedule immediate follow-up tasks for post-incident: prefix prefetch quota, add alert for prefix-cardinality spike, and small guard in router to reject >X distinct prefixes/min.

kai: noted. I'll stay on this thread and run the handoff in 30m. I'll prepare the short incident summary for SRE rotation and mark sov-owner. Also creating a temporary dashboard tile for tenant-42.

lucas: drafting customer-facing snippet for Jen: "We're aware of elevated errors impacting some read requests for your workspace. We've applied emergency throttles and a targeted cache-mode change to prevent incorrect responses while we investigate. We'll follow up with a timeline and root cause." Want to add any SLA language?

jen: that wording is fine, keep it concise. I'll send to acme-inc and partnerX now and note that we will follow up with a technical write-up.

ops-bot: Monitoring update (10m): error-rate trending down, origin CPU plateauing at +18%. Canary hosts healthy. Rolling mitigation to 50% of hosts.

incident-bot: Handoff reminder: @kai please hand off to @sylvia in 30m. Postmortem owner: kai. Action items assigned: sylvia (alert + router guard), matt (cache-eviction patch PR), jen (customer comms), lucas (post-incident exec summary).

kai: handoff plan: 1) hold current mitigations for 30m, 2) if error-rate <10% over 15m keep reduced quota + scoped bypass and start controlled reinstate of routing weight, 3) if CPU >85% rollback bypass and increase throttle to 15%. I'll capture timeline in the handoff note.

sylvia: noted, I'll pick up after the 30m. Also creating a short runbook entry for "prefix flood - snapback" so oncall future can act faster.

matt: quick follow-up: opened PR for a small cache eviction guard to avoid repeated prefetch churn: https://git.internal/redwood/eviction-guard/pull/88 (tests + canary config).

jen: sent initial comms to impacted accounts. will update when we have final RCA.

incident-bot: THREAD CLOSED FOR NOW: mitigation in progress. next_update in 30m or on-change.
